practiceReport.archetypeNote: Perimeter speed/cut position (WR) — requires full deceleration/burst clearance on lower-body tags (76% Questionable baseline).
practiceReport.beatComment: Watkins may have injured his groin during the 49ers' 35-10 win over the Vikings in Week 11, when he hauled in his lone target for 19 yards while playing 28 snaps on offense. His practice participation over the next two days will shed light on his status heading into Sunday's NFC West tilt against the Seahawks. If Watkins cannot play in Week 12, then Keenan Allen, Jacob Cowing and Demarcus Robinson would all be in line for larger roles on offense.

practiceReport.name: Brock Purdy
practiceReport.archetypeNote: High availability prior; rarely misses starts if throwing full velocity by Thursday.
practiceReport.beatComment: Purdy put on a master class during this past Sunday's 35-10 win against the Vikings in Mexico City, completing 21 of 26 passes for 255 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions. Now with a health concern in tow, his status will be monitored closely to get a sense of his odds to suit up Sunday against the Seahawks. Mac Jones is waiting in the wings in the event Purdy isn't able to play in Week 12.

practiceReport.name: Mike Evans
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Veteran X-receiver toughness prior; routinely manages Wednesday reps but requires soft-tissue/Achilles sprint clearance.
factors: Did Not Participate (DNP) on Wednesday (veteran maintenance profile, awaiting Thursday workload)
practiceReport.beatComment: After a three-game (and four-week) absence due to right Achilles tendinitis, Evans returned to action during Sunday's win against the Vikings in Mexico City, recording a 43 percent offensive snap share and gathering in six of seven targets for 109 yards and one touchdown. The 49ers likely are managing Evans' workload to begin Week 12 prep, but his status nonetheless will be monitored in advance of Sunday's contest against the Seahawks.

practiceReport.name: Keenan Allen
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Perimeter speed/cut position (WR) — requires full deceleration/burst clearance on lower-body tags (76% Questionable baseline).
factors: Habitual Veteran Rest prior (Keenan Allen maintenance schedule)
practiceReport.beatComment: Sunday marked Allen's first time working with Mike Evans, the 49ers' top wide receiver, and the latter dominated the attention of QB Brock Purdy, posting a 6-109-1 line on seven targets in his first game action since Week 6. If Evans' Achilles issue flares up at any point, Allen may be thrust into WR1 duties, which could yield more consistent results as he becomes more acclimated to head coach Kyle Shanahan's offense. For now, though, Allen will play a distant second to Evans for as long as the latter is healthy and available.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Austen Pleasants
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Pleasants opened the regular season on injured reserve due to a knee injury that he sustained in a preseason game against the Chargers in late August. He was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, and he would need to be activated from injured reserve in order to be available for Sunday's game against the Seahawks. With Colton McKivitz (ankle) out for the rest of the season, Pleasants would be a candidate to start at right tackle once he's removed from IR.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Christian Kirk
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: After he had missed the 49ers' first six games of the season while recovering from a calf injury, Kirk landed on injured reserve for the second time this season back on Nov. 7 due to a right knee injury sustained in his team debut Week 7 in Atlanta. Since Kirk didn't specify whether he required a partial meniscectomy or a meniscus repair, his exact recovery timeline isn't known. Regardless, he'll have to miss at least two more games while he's on IR.

irAndReserveTracker.name: De'Zhaun Stribling
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Week 8 Bye excluded from NFL 4-game minimum count
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Stribling was diagnosed with a deltoid sprain of his left ankle after getting injured in the 49ers' Week 1 win over the Rams in Australia and underwent surgery Sept. 16. The 23-year-old was handed an estimated recovery timeline of about 10 weeks, leaving the 49ers optimistic that he would be ready to play at some point in December. While Shanahan indicated that Stribling's timeline doesn't appear to have changed, the young wideout will need to get back on the practice field before the 49ers can hone in on a more precise target date for him to resume playing. Given the haziness of his return date along with the fact that he could face limitations with his snaps once activated, Stribling likely isn't worth holding in redraft leagues at this point in the season.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Sam Okuayinonu
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Okuayinonu suffered a broken foot in practice ahead of Week 1 and required surgery. He appears to be making progress and could return at some point before the end of the regular season. The 28-year-old appeared in 15 regular-season games last season, and made 12 starts and recorded 23 tackles (16 solo), including 3.0 sacks, and a forced fumble.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Isaac Guerendo
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Week 8 Bye excluded from NFL 4-game minimum count
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Guerendo has been on the PUP list with a pec injury since training camp, but it now looks like he may be making some progress toward returning to action. Even if he does get back to full strength at some point soon, though, it's not clear how much room there will be for him in a 49ers' backfield that has recently been dominated by veteran Christian McCaffrey and rookie third-rounder Kaelon Black.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Nick Martin
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Martin opened the regular season on injured reserve due to a hamstring injury that he sustained during training camp in August. Shanahan said Martin is "getting close" to returning to practice, and if he's cleared for field work this week, his participation level will shed light on whether he'll play in Week 6 against the Commanders on Monday, Oct. 19. The 2025 third-rounder logged 11 tackles (eight solo) and one fumble recovery across seven regular-season games during his rookie campaign, which he finished on injured reserve due to a concussion.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Alfred Collins
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: This move was anticipated, as Collins is set to miss the entire 2026 campaign as a result of tearing his patellar tendon during practice Tuesday. Osa Odighizuwa, CJ West and Gracen Halton should get plenty of reps at defensive tackle with Collins and Sam Okuayinonu (foot) sidelined.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Andrew Farmer II
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Farmer was not picked up by another squad after the 49ers waived him with an injury designation earlier in the week, and now he'll be required to stay on the team's IR list for the year unless he negotiates an injury settlement. He last played regular-season snaps in 2023 with the Chargers.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Colton McKivitz
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: McKivitz was diagnosed with a fractured and dislocated ankle that he sustained in the 49ers' Week 11 win over the Vikings. He's expected to miss the rest of the 2026 season, and Vederian Lowe is expected to take over as the starter at right tackle in McKivitz's absence.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Darrick Forrest
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: It's not clear what kind of injury Forrest is dealing with, but he's now on track to spend the entire 2026 season on IR unless he negotiates an injury settlement with the 49ers. His absence could open up more opportunities for rookie undrafted free agents Jalen Stroman and Larry Worth.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Gracen Halton
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Halton will be sidelined for the rest of the 2026 season, but the rookie fourth-rounder is expected to be back for OTAs in May. He'll end his first NFL campaign with 15 tackles (nine solo), including 2.0 sacks, one pass defense and a scoop-and-score across eight regular-season games.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Jake Tonges
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: The team placed Tonges on injured reserve earlier Wednesday, and now it's official that he will miss the rest of the season. Tonges suffered an MCL tear in the season opener against the Rams. Jack Stoll was signed to the practice squad to add depth, and Luke Farrell now projects to be the second tight end behind George Kittle.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Mikail Kamara
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Placed on Injured Reserve (Knee) on Aug 3, 2026; ineligible to return in 2026 under NFL CBA rules.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Nick Zakelj
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: The nature of Zakelj's injury is unclear, as is when he exactly picked up the injury. However, by being placed on IR without a designation to return, the 2022 sixth-rounder will be forced to miss the entire upcoming season unless he reached an injury settlement with San Francisco.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Ricky Pearsall
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: The procedure typically carries a wide-ranging recovery timeline of 6-to-12 months, so while Pearsall will be ruled out for the season, it's not clear if he'll be available for the start of the 49ers' offseason program next spring or the start of training camp next summer. The wideout will wind up having played in just 20 of a possible 51 regular-season contests and one of two playoff games through his first three NFL campaigns, missing time as a rookie while recovering from a gunshot wound to the chest before being hampered by the PCL injury off and on in 2025. He'll turn 27 in September and will be entering the final season of his rookie contract in 2027.
